tldr: This is a loose cluster of mostly arXiv papers that share policy- and preference-optimization vocabulary, not one developing story. It began with RL recipes for agents, preference-optimization variants and kernel-tuning agents, then drifted toward vision-language hallucination fixes and benchmarks for visual agents.
whats_new: Nov 18: Einsia AI announced Visual Cipher Bench for long-horizon visual reasoning in agents, joining PhysScope and MM-ReportBench in a week of multimodal-agent evaluation work.
why_it_matters: If you ship agents that read screens, diagrams or images, the evidence here is about grounding failures (answering from priors instead of the pixels), and every result is author-reported on the papers' own benchmarks, not production evidence.

beats.headline: RL recipes target the hard parts of training agents: delayed credit, orchestration and partial verifiers
beats.summary: TSBPO, few-step flow RL, CRESiST for speech translation, learned multi-agent orchestration, and negative-only policy optimization.

beats.headline: Preference-optimization papers target general preferences, shifting objectives, noisy labels and missing gold answers
beats.summary: DNO empirical study, preference learning from multi-agent debate, steerable multi-objective GRPO with LoRA adapters, and PORT token reweighting.

beats.headline: Agents that tune GPU kernels and AI infrastructure get methods and benchmarks
beats.summary: Question-driven kernel agents, a local 7B CUDA study, Infrathon, and the Ascend NPU benchmark AscendGYM.

beats.headline: The cluster shifts to vision-language models that hallucinate objects or reason past what they see
beats.summary: MIRA, latent multimodal reasoning, VIGOR, cross-modal unlearning, VEPO, GEM-MM and severity-aware preference validation.

beats.headline: Optimization papers on routing, merchandising and federated learning ride along on shared vocabulary
beats.summary: Small-model capability routing, cold-start cover-photo selection, parallel split learning, and explainable federated learning.

beats.headline: Visual-agent benchmarks pile up: decoys, web tasks, physics diagrams, reports and cipher puzzles
beats.summary: Elorian's decoy test, Google's Multimodal Knowledge Agent Benchmark, Vision-as-a-Tool, WebArena-Pro, ViRA, MM-ReportBench, PhysScope and Visual Cipher Bench.

open_questions: Does any independent group reproduce TSBPO's gains on long-horizon agent tasks outside the paper's own environments?
Does negative-only policy optimization train useful agents when the verifier can only reject wrong answers in real tool-use settings?
Do kernel-optimization agents beat vendor libraries and hand-tuned kernels on Infrathon or AscendGYM workloads under their cost accounting?
Do the VLM hallucination fixes (VEPO, GEM-MM, severity-aware alignment) hold up on screenshots and documents rather than natural photos?
Will Visual Cipher Bench publish tasks, scoring code and model results, or stay an announcement?
Does external visual tooling (Vision-as-a-Tool, zooming in ViRA) beat a stronger base model's own vision on WebArena-Pro-style tasks?
take_for_builders: If your agent reads screens or images, add eval cases where the obvious prior answer is wrong (decoys, altered diagrams) before trusting a new VLM or alignment recipe; for kernel-tuning agents, gate every change on a correctness check and compare against your vendor-library baseline.
